title: Toolchain
description: The marker `xplainer setup` leaves behind, and the first thing `xplainer daemon install` reads. ADR 0020 §Ordering fixes both its existence and its job: install "checks a marker written by `setup` (`toolchain.json`, recording the Chrome Headless Shell and TTS versions, paths and checksums), verifies the recorded paths still exist, and on failure exits 3 having written nothing" — because neither `install` nor the daemon ever downloads, so a machine whose render toolchain is absent must be told at install time rather than three days later inside a render. It lives at `<state dir>/toolchain.json`. It is a checked contract rather than a private file because three surfaces read it and none of them owns it: `setup` writes it, install's read-only preflight validates it, and `daemon update`'s compatibility check judges it against what an incoming runtime requires. It records the binaries a render needs — the Chrome Headless Shell that draws every frame, the speech synthesiser every narration goes through and, from `format_version` 2, the FFmpeg every render pipes its frames to — each with the route that acquired it, because the routes are not interchangeable and none of them can be inferred from what is on disk. The schema decides what a document may say and not what a render needs: `ffmpeg` is optional here, and whether its absence stops a render is the gate's judgement (ADR 0031 §Note, 2026-11-12, D1 and D12). Every path in it is absolute and resolved on the machine it describes — a marker copied to another machine names files that are not there, which is precisely what the preflight's existence check catches.

format_version.description: The shape of this document. `2` is what this build writes: `chrome` and `speech`, an optional `ffmpeg`, and no `workspace`. `1` is the shape every release before ADR 0031's cut wrote, with a required `workspace` and no `ffmpeg`; it still validates here and this build still reads it, as a valid document describing an incomplete toolchain. The two are not interchangeable across a daemon: a runtime records the format it reads, and an update or a `setup` that would leave a version-2 marker under a version-1 daemon is refused, because crossing the cut is a reinstall. A version this build does not know is a rollback signal and never corruption: the marker is preserved and the reader says which version it met, the same rule the job store applies to a record written by a newer daemon.

created_at.description: When `setup` finished acquiring what is recorded below. RFC 3339, so a support report can say how old the toolchain is without the file's mtime, which a copy or a restore rewrites.

ToolchainComponent.title: ToolchainComponent
ToolchainComponent.description: One acquired component: what it is, where it ended up, what it hashed to, and which route brought it. Most routes acquire one file and `path` names it. A route that acquires several — the in-process ONNX speech path needs a model graph, a voice tensor and a platform runtime, and no one of them is the component — also records `files`, so that a reader checking that what `setup` produced is still here checks all of it rather than the one artefact `path` happened to name.

version.description: The version acquired, exactly as its own provider spells it. Compared as a string and never parsed: an upgrade is reported to the user, and the daemon never applies one itself.

path.description: The absolute path this component was resolved to. `install` checks that it still exists before it registers anything, which is the difference between "setup has been run" and "setup has been run and its results are still here".

sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the acquired artefact, lowercase hex, as verified against the expected digest the toolchain manifest carries for this platform. Recorded so a later check can tell a replaced binary from a missing one.

provider.description: Which route acquired this component — `manifest` for the Chrome for Testing build the toolchain manifest's row for this platform names, and `docker`, `bundle`, `url` or `onnx` for the four speech routes. A machine-readable token rather than prose, because `status` branches on it and a remediation that named the wrong route would send a user to reinstall something they never installed.

files.description: Every file this component is made of, where it is made of more than the one `path` names. Optional, and absent for every route that acquires a single artefact — which is why adding it did not move `format_version`: a build that does not read it still finds everything it needs, and a build that does reads a strictly larger set. It is a **small, named** set and never a tree inventory: the four artefacts the ONNX speech route pins, not the several thousand files inside an unpacked bundle. Its purpose is the existence check ADR 0020 §Ordering requires of `daemon install` — "verifies the recorded paths still exist" — which for a multi-file component is only meaningful if every path is recorded. The digests make the same check able to tell a replaced file from a missing one, and are what a warm cache is re-verified against instead of being trusted. It carries no `minItems`, deliberately: a provider that records the field and then leaves it empty is caught by a runtime assertion beside the provider that knows how many files its own route has, and a schema keyword would instead have made the shape depend on `provider` — a conditional, which is the one construct the codegen splitter handles badly.

ToolchainFile.title: ToolchainFile
ToolchainFile.description: One file a multi-file component is made of, and the two facts that let a later run decide whether it is still the file that was acquired.

path.description: The absolute path on this machine, resolved the same way and for the same reason as the component's own `path`.

sha256.description: The SHA-256 of this file, lowercase hex. For a file fetched whole it is the reviewed digest it was admitted on; for a file taken out of a verified archive it is the digest of what came out, recorded so a later run can detect drift in a file whose archive is long gone.

bytes.description: Its length. Recorded so a check can refuse a truncated or replaced file on a `stat` rather than by hashing a hundred megabytes, and so a report can say how much of the disk the component is.

ToolchainFfmpeg.title: ToolchainFfmpeg
ToolchainFfmpeg.description: The FFmpeg executable every render pipes its frames to, and what `setup` proved about it. A separate definition rather than a `ToolchainComponent`, because that one is `additionalProperties: false` and shared by `chrome` and `speech`, and making these fields conditional on which component it is would be the construct the codegen splitter handles badly. Optional at the root, so that a marker written before FFmpeg was acquired is still a document every reader can parse; a build that renders with it treats its absence as an incomplete toolchain.

version.description: The token after `ffmpeg version ` on the first line of `ffmpeg -version`, exactly as the build spells it — `9.0.2`, `n9.0.2-39-g7adfbe40dc-20261031`. Reported, never parsed: capability is judged on `libavcodec`.

path.description: The absolute path of the executable a render spawns, resolved on this machine. Never looked up on `PATH` at render time: what `setup` probed is what runs.

sha256.description: For `manifest`: the archive's reviewed digest, as for Chrome. For `path`: the executable's own digest when `setup` probed it — recorded rather than expected, so it detects later drift and proves nothing about provenance.

provider.description: Which route recorded it — `manifest` for the pinned build the toolchain manifest's row for this platform names, `path` for an executable named with `setup --ffmpeg-path`. There is no route that finds one on `PATH` by itself.

files.description: The executable **first**, with its own digest and length — the manifest row's reviewed `member_sha256` for `manifest`, the probed digest for `path` — followed by whatever was kept beside it, such as the licence text and the provenance record. `files[0].bytes` is what the stat-only check compares, so a replaced binary is `toolchain_stale` without hashing it. `minItems` is safe here, unlike on `ToolchainComponent.files`, because every route records the executable, so the constraint does not depend on the route.

libavcodec.description: The libavcodec version the executable reported it had loaded, `major.minor.micro`, so a build that raises its floor can judge a recorded component without running it. The floor is judged on the major alone.

licence.description: The licence the build's own `configure` declared, as an SPDX id — `GPL-3.0-or-later`, `GPL-2.0-or-later`, `LGPL-2.1-or-later`, `LGPL-3.0-or-later`. For `manifest` it is the row's, cross-checked against `probe.license` and `probe.buildconf` before anything is recorded; `status` prints it.

publisher.description: Who published the artefact, as the allowlist in code maps the row's URL prefix — never a value the manifest supplied. Absent for `path`, which no publisher vouches for.

source_url.description: Where the corresponding source of that build is published, when its row names one. Recorded so that the licence obligation travels with the binary rather than with a manifest the machine may never read again.

ToolchainFfmpegProbe.title: ToolchainFfmpegProbe
ToolchainFfmpegProbe.description: What the executable said about itself when `setup` probed it, one array entry per line of output, as it printed them. Kept verbatim rather than summarised so that a support report, or a later build with a different question, can read the answer without running the binary again.

version.description: `ffmpeg -version`: the version line, the configuration and the library versions `libavcodec` is read from.

buildconf.description: `ffmpeg -buildconf`: the `configure` flags the build was made with, which is what says which encoders and which licence configuration it carries.

license.description: `ffmpeg -L`: the licence the build itself states. Spelled `license` because it is the name of the flag; the field it is checked against is `licence`.

ToolchainWorkspace.title: ToolchainWorkspace
ToolchainWorkspace.description: **Deprecated: written by `format_version` 1 only.** The workspace payload's own identity — which platform it was resolved for, and which template it resolved — from the releases that installed a render workspace through `setup --workspace`. No render reads that workspace and this build neither writes nor judges this field; it stays in the schema, optional, so that a version-1 marker still validates.

platform.description: `<platform>-<arch>` as the payload's manifest records it — `darwin-arm64`, `linux-x64`, `win32-x64`. A workspace holds compiled dependencies, so a payload resolved for another platform is a different artefact even when every declared version matches.

version.description: The version of the workspace template this payload resolved. It is the template package's own version and not a pin, so a reader comparing pins reads the payload's manifest; this field says which template the pins came from.
